title: How Does Face ID Actually Know It's You?
sources: Apple Support, 'About Face ID advanced technology' (support.apple.com/102381): the TrueDepth camera projects and analyzes thousands of invisible dots to create a depth map of your face and also captures an infrared image; works even in total darkness; it is attention-aware and recognizes if your eyes are open; Face ID always requires depth information, which isn't found in print or 2D digital photographs; Face ID data, including mathematical representations of your face, is encrypted and protected by the Secure Enclave and doesn't leave your device; the chance a random person could unlock it is less than 1 in 1,000,000; the probability is higher for twins and siblings that look like you and among children under 13

Apple, 'Face ID Security' guide (Nov 2017, iPhone X): the dot projector projects and reads over 30,000 infrared dots to form a depth map of the face; detects that your eyes are open and directed at your device; data never leaves the device

lines.text: How does your phone know it's your face, and not a photo of you?
lines.caps: HOW DOES YOUR *PHONE | KNOW IT'S YOUR *FACE | AND NOT A *PHOTO | OF *YOU?

lines.text: Well, a tiny projector above the screen
sprays thousands of invisible infrared dots across your face,
and a special camera reads where each one lands.
lines.caps: AND A SPECIAL *CAMERA | READS *WHERE | EACH ONE *LANDS

lines.text: Dots on your nose land closer than dots on your cheeks,
lines.caps: DOTS ON YOUR *NOSE | LAND *CLOSER | THAN DOTS ON YOUR *CHEEKS

lines.text: so the pattern becomes a 3D map of your face.
lines.caps: SO THE *PATTERN | BECOMES A *3D MAP | OF YOUR *FACE

lines.text: That's why a flat photo fails: it has no depth.
lines.caps: THAT'S WHY A *FLAT | *PHOTO FAILS | IT HAS NO *DEPTH

lines.text: It even checks that your eyes are open,
then saves your face as math, locked inside the phone.
lines.caps: THEN SAVES YOUR *FACE | AS *MATH | LOCKED *INSIDE | THE *PHONE

lines.text: A random stranger? Less than a one in a million chance.
lines.caps: A RANDOM *STRANGER? | LESS THAN *ONE | IN A *MILLION | *CHANCE

lines.text: But the twist? An identical twin might just unlock it,
lines.caps: BUT THE *TWIST? | AN IDENTICAL *TWIN | MIGHT JUST *UNLOCK IT

lines.text: because to your phone, they look almost exactly like you.
lines.caps: BECAUSE TO YOUR *PHONE | THEY LOOK *ALMOST | EXACTLY LIKE *YOU
